title: Streaming: KV cache oscillation causing chunk loss (scratchpad)
content:
Context / symptom summary:
- Intermittent missing chunks / truncated streaming responses observed under a specific traffic pattern (bursty short requests + long-context requests).
- Happens primarily on dedicated pools running 4x A100, when model uses KV cache (larger context usage > 4k).
- Client sees final "done" event sometimes, but several earlier data chunks never arrive. No 5xx returned.
- Correlated with sudden KV-cache eviction cycles (observed in node logs). Suspect oscillation between caching states triggers internal backpressure that causes chunk drops.

Notes to self (logs I captured):
- Server log snippets around one incident (timestamps trimmed):
  [2026-03-09T15:21:42Z] INFO: request start id=8a3f kv_cache:hit keys=1
  [2026-03-09T15:21:43Z] WARN: kv_cache:evicting 128 entries (policy=adaptive) pool=dedicated-4xa100
  [2026-03-09T15:21:43Z] INFO: batching: flush id=8a3f size=1 latency=1ms
  [2026-03-09T15:21:43Z] ERROR: stream: write chunk failed id=8a3f err=write tcp 10.0.0.23:443->10.1.2.45:51234: connection reset by peer
  [2026-03-09T15:21:43Z] INFO: request end id=8a3f status=200 streamed=true tokens=76
  Observations: error appears immediately after eviction; connection reset by peer could be client disconnect but client shows still connected.

Client-side capture (python SSE reader I used):
- Script: simple EventSource-ish read using requests + iter_lines to measure gaps.
- Repro run: 50 sequentials, interleaved small prompts (<=64 tokens) with 1 large warmup (2k context).
- Example output: several runs show long gaps and then sudden stream closure without terminal chunk.

Commands and repro steps I used:
1) Lightweight SSE probe (bash):
   for i in {1..50}; do 
     curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
       -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
       -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=rw-llama-13b-kv" \
       -d '{"prompt":"tell me a short story\n","max_tokens":150,"stream":true}' \
       | awk 'BEGIN{RS="\n\n"} {print NR" chunk:"substr($0,1,80)}' &
     sleep 0.3
   done
   wait
- Pattern: bursts of overlapping connections + many active KV entries. Failures appear at ~30-40 concurrent bursts.

2) Controlled single-connection stress with ramping context (python):
   - open connection, send 100 small prompts sequentially over same connection (function-calling style) with increasing context (append previous outputs).
   - measure time between chunks and count missing sequence IDs.

3) Server-side repro using vegeta to emulate bursty small requests mixed with single long request. Vegeta target file attached to linked ticket.

Error snippets captured on server stdout: 
- "kv_cache: eviction spike: current_entries=8192 target=4096"
- "stream: stalled write; sendq=2048 pending_bytes=131072"
- "runtime: background worker busy; kv-reload stuck 1200ms"
- occasional: "epoll wait returned EINTR" (might be red herring)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache eviction triggers synchronous work on main serving thread (lock/GC) that temporarily stalls streaming writer; when stall resolves, buffered chunks are dropped due to internal buffer limits or because writer state was reset.
2) Backpressure path incorrectly treats ephemeral client slowness vs internal stalled writer; eviction event flips a flag that cancels streaming writes for in-flight requests.
3) Send buffer accounting bug: after eviction we call shrink_buffers() which inadvertently sets pending_bytes to 0 while sendq still holds older buffers, leading to false impression buffer is free and subsequent writes are not queued (dropped).
4) Client disconnects coincidentally; but multiple clients show same pattern so server-side root cause more likely.

What I tried already (and results):
- Increasing internal sendq threshold from 512KB -> 2MB on a canary build: incidence reduced but not eliminated. Suggests threshold tuning masks but not root cause.
- Disabled synchronous eviction (made eviction async): seemed to reduce frequency significantly in local perf runs.
- Reproduced using both hosted and dedicated with slightly different timings; dedicated > frequency.
- Added extra logging in stream writer: when eviction starts set flag; observed that writer drops writes when flag toggles mid-request (found in logs).

Immediate next steps (practical):
- Add deterministic test harness that reproduces eviction spike deterministically: create N small requests to fill KV, then force long request to create eviction. Verify with unit/regression harness.
- Instrument writer state machine to log transitions and queue sizes (already partial). Short-term: add counters to determine if write attempted after queue overflow.
- Re-run with kernel-level TCPSEND buffer tracing (ss -i) to see if OS-level drops occur.
- Ask SRE to run flamegraphs around eviction time to see blocking stacks (ticket created).

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Make eviction purely off-main-thread; batch apply to avoid stalls.
- Ensure writer is resilient to transient lock blocking: buffer writes to temporary per-request queue and flush after critical section.
- Add stronger backpressure signal to clients (e.g., send an interim keepalive event) so client-side doesn't reset connection prematurely.

Questions for Diego / Lin:
- Diego: can you double-check the buffer accounting logic in net/writer.go around shrink_buffers()? The code touched by PR #1452 looks suspicious.
- Lin: can you run the new async-eviction branch on the dedicated-4xa100 canary for a day and report incidents? Is there any perf/regression impact?

Random notes / lines I may want later:
- client-side hack for now: on reconnect, ask for missing tokens via a follow-up delta endpoint; not ideal but reduces customer-visible truncations.
- TTL for KV cache entries currently 24h; eviction based on memory heuristics. Maybe reduce aggressiveness for streaming-heavy workloads.

Raw client example (python SSE probe):
import requests, time
url = "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=rw-llama-13b-kv"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY')}", "Accept": "text/event-stream"}
with requests.post(url, json={"prompt":"x","stream":True}, headers=headers, stream=True) as r:
    for line in r.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True):
        if line:
            print(time.time(), line[:120])

Final: Save all collected logs to GCS path gs://redwood-debug/kv-oscillation/2026-03-09/ and attach to JIRA INF-4392.

TODO checklist:
- [ ] deterministic harness (unit test)
- [ ] more writer logs + counters
- [ ] run async-eviction branch on canary pool
- [ ] SRE flamegraph capture at incident time
- [ ] decide on short-term client mitigation

-- Aisha
